When playing in a Musical Reality, the following mechanics apply by default: •Musical Numbers: Any character may initiate a song or dance number to express thoughts, feelings, or intentions, providing bonuses to actions taken during or immediately after the performance.
•Characters can incorporate dance into movements, gaining bonuses or defensive benefits. •Reward creative descriptions with mechanical bonuses, keeping checks simple (DC 10-15).

In musical realities, characters can declare a dramatic moment once per session, emphasizing heightened emotional storytelling: •Choose an appropriate dramatic moment or reveal. •Spend 2 EE and roll a Performance check (DC 12). ◦ Success: Inspire allies, granting each one Advantage on their next roll. ◦ Great Success (DC 18): Additionally, restore 2 EE to each ally. ◦ Failure: Still grants inspiration, but the GM introduces a minor complication.

•Action Type: Group Action (initiated by spending 3 EE) •Up to 3 allies can join your performance as a reaction. Each participant rolls a Performance check: ◦ Individual Success(DC 10+): Grants the entire group +1 to checks related to the performance's goal. ◦ Failure: No penalty, but no bonus granted by the character. •Outcome: If the majority succeed, the GM awards a narrative or mechanical bonus relevant to the theme (e.g., persuasion, motivation, stealth, morale, or inspiration). Initiate a Group Performance, granting allies within earshot or sight a bonus to their next check, equal to your Charisma modifier, provided they actively participate in the song/dance.

records.proposedName: Comprehensive Mechanics and Rules for the Sideralis Branch
records.summary: Sideralis is a branch of unrelenting chaos, where the natural laws of physics, time, and space are in constant flux. This instability manifests in every aspect of the realities within Sideralis, from shifting gravity fields to temporal loops and spontaneous elemental outbreaks. Gameplay in Sideralis revolves around embracing and surviving the unpredictable. Characters must adapt quickly, think creatively, and use chaos to their advantage. ---

- What They Are: When an action or event occurs that could influence the emotional tone of a reality— such as a charismatic speech, a devastating loss, or a hopeful celebration—the GM calls for an Emotional Resonance Check.

- After finding a grove of “Blazing Orchids,” a flower that generates intense heat without burning, the players successfully harvest several blooms. - Using a combination of Alchemy (DC 14) and Engineering (DC 15), they craft a “Thermal Lens” attachment for their long-range scope. This lens allows them to see heat signatures through solid objects, giving them a tactical advantage in combat. Scenario 4: Mutations from Prolonged Exposure - The group sets up a long-term camp near a crystalline lake that constantly forms and dissolves structures of glowing quartz. - After a few days, one character gains a minor mutation: their skin glows faintly in the dark, allowing them to see without light but also making them easier to detect. - The GM decides this mutation lasts as long as the character remains in Vitaevox, adding a unique trait to their adventuring experience. --- Integration into Campaigns - Exploration and Discovery Focus: Players are constantly presented with new phenomena, keeping the gameplay fresh and full of surprises. - Resource-Driven Gameplay: The branchʼs generative nature rewards creative resource use, crafting, and adaptation. - Cultural Interaction and Roleplay: Many quests involve interacting with unique civilizations, encouraging social and diplomatic skills. - Environmental Adaptation: The constantly shifting landscapes mean players must think on their feet and adapt to changing circumstances.

- The party locates an abandoned assembly line and finds a blueprint for a flamethrower powered by steam vents. - They need to gather specific materials scattered across the factory floor. Using Survival and Investigation checks, they locate enough components. - They roll Intelligence (Engineering) checks to construct the weapon. On a success, they have a powerful tool for the next encounter; on a failure, they must spend additional time repairing their mistakes, risking more encounters with security forces.

The volcano can erupt at any time. Roll a d20 every hour; on a 1 or 2, the volcano becomes active. Characters within 1 mile must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 16) to avoid 3d6 fire damage from falling magma or debris.

•Magma Flows: Approaching within 10 feet of a magma flow requires Constitution saving throws (DC 15) every 5 minutes to avoid 1d6 fire damage from radiant heat. Failure results in falling prone and taking 1d4 bludgeoning damage.

Toxic gases, such as sulfur dioxide, drift through the area. Characters exposed must make Constitution saving throws (DC 13) every 10 minutes or suffer 1 level of exhaustion. Prolonged exposure (more than 1 hour) requires Constitution saving throws (DC 15) against the poisoned condition.

•Characters attempting to ascend or descend steep volcanic slopes must make Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 14) to avoid losing their footing. Failure results in a slide back down, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage.
